brand.name: Milo
brand.uiNameRule: Milo appears in the mark only; app UI titles use the descriptive tool name without a Milo text prefix.

requiredUiRules.description: PDF reports follow Milo CI, including product name, shared colors, typography, source, app version and page numbering. Render and visually verify representative pages.
All exports, CLI/API outputs and archive members identify their source. Related artifacts share a meaningful basename with relevant processing parameters. Test actual download names.
Charts, spectra, bars, lines and report graphics use the Milo chart palette instead of library default colors such as brown or generic green.
Every Milo app shows its own version in the topbar, right side, next to status.
Command-line style activity output is hidden by default, collapsible, or placed in its own Activity/Runs/Logs tab.
Use the Milo mark as the visible product-family signal. App UI titles use descriptive tool names without a Milo text prefix.
Selected segmented or toggle-style buttons use Milo teal instead of the dark ink/topbar color.
Every Milo app with authentication has a visible topbar logout button and automatically logs out inactive users.
Downstream projects use Milo CI as source-of-truth guidance, but production builds must not depend on the local Milo CI project folder.
requiredUiRules.requiredPractice: Copy or vendor required CI files and assets into the downstream project before build or deployment.

requiredUiRules.description: Native HTML hidden must always keep elements invisible, even when ci-* component classes define display: flex, grid, block or inline-flex.
The official Milo mark includes the small robot plus a visible Milo wordmark below it. Do not duplicate Milo as a text prefix in the topbar title.
Process steps must share a stable workspace, top process navigation, reserved dynamic regions, responsive minimum sizes and no automatic scroll jumps on normal selection changes.
Image, video, audio and document tools keep the subject reference visible in a stable preview frame; finished output replaces the reference in the same slot.
Loading, analyzing, creating, checking, complete and error states are integrated into the existing layout; inputs/results remain on error and duplicate jobs are prevented.
AI actions use a recognizable Sparkles or magic-wand icon, tooltip, accessible label, stable dimensions and non-destructive suggestion adoption.
Dark Mode is the Milo UI default as Milo Night Workbench. Light Mode is available only as an intentional opt-in via data-ci-theme="light". Both modes use the same ci-* components and central tokens.
requiredUiRules.requiredAttribute: none for dark default; data-ci-theme="light" for opt-in light mode

requiredUiRules.description: The standard Milo mark keeps the original dark Milo figure on a white tile for the default Night Workbench. Use assets/milo-mark-light.svg for explicit light contexts.
Buttons, inputs, selects, textareas, segmented controls, icon buttons, AI actions and process steps use shared Milo control tokens for height, radius, padding, gap, borders and states.

Every ci-mark usage renders the official assets/milo-mark.svg: dark Milo figure on a white tile with visible Milo wordmark. Deprecated bar fallbacks and recolored mark variants are not used in app UI.
Reusable Milo mark graphics are exported from the official mark into SVG, PNG and JPG variants. Alpha variants are available where the format supports transparency; JPG is white background only.
Authenticated Milo apps use the Animation-style login layout: centered card, official Milo mark, concise context, labeled inputs and one primary login action.
Deployable Milo web apps provide an Apple Touch Icon and web app manifest so iPhone home screen bookmarks use the Milo mark.
Browser tabs use the current Milo icon through SVG favicon plus PNG and ICO fallbacks. Favicon links include a version query to avoid stale cached older icons.

Long-running, costly, asynchronous or editorial workflows use durable job IDs, autosave, resume, idempotency, explicit suggestion adoption, versioned results, clear error causes and visible download/export actions.
Updating or deploying a Milo UI is complete only when the target project has migrated affected real app pages and tools/check-adoption.mjs passes without failures.

summary: Added a reusable Milo CI adoption checker for target projects.
Made copying vendored CI files insufficient without migrating and checking real app pages.
Documented checker failures as blockers for commits, tags, staging, production and redeployments.
downstreamActions: Do not treat copied vendored CI files as a completed Milo CI update.
Migrate affected real app pages to the current Milo CI rules.
Run tools/check-adoption.mjs against the target project after every Milo CI update and before release or deployment.
Fix all checker failures before commit, tag, stage, production or redeployment.
Review warnings and either fix them or document the project-specific exception.

summary: Set Milo Night Workbench as the default UI mode with light mode as opt-in.
Added stable process UX, durable workflow UX, unified controls, login layout, home screen icons and current favicon assets.
Provided generated Milo mark graphics and consistency tests for downstream apps.
downstreamActions: Use durable job IDs and idempotency keys for long-running, costly or asynchronous actions.
Persist sources, inputs, app version, CI version and relevant rule/config versions with each job.
Resume or re-query existing jobs after reload, login or unclear server responses before creating new variants.
Keep suggestions as explicit candidates with accept, reject and compare actions.
Keep previous inputs, snapshots and results visible on errors or rule changes.
Show clear error causes and visible download/export actions in the app UI.
Run tests/workflow-resilience-playwright.js before UI release.
Adopt dark Milo Night Workbench as the default UI without a theme attribute.
Use data-ci-theme="light" only for intentional light-mode contexts.
Update vendored assets/milo-mark.svg and add assets/milo-mark-light.svg for light contexts.
Keep Milo unchanged in character: original dark figure on a white tile.
Verify dark UI on desktop, small laptop and mobile before release.
Adopt ci-process and ci-process-bar for multi-step flows.
Use ci-media-workbench and ci-preview-frame for image, video, audio and document tools.
Move loading, validation, suggestions, errors and progress into reserved regions instead of replacing the whole workspace.
Use ci-ai-action with Sparkles or magic-wand icons and explicit suggestion adoption.
Run the process stability Playwright regression before UI release.
Update vendored tokens.css and ci.css.
Replace local button, input, select, segmented and icon-button styling with Milo control classes.
Use ci-button-block for full-width primary actions.
Remove local border-radius and height overrides from standard controls.
Run the controls consistency Playwright regression before UI release.
Render the official assets/milo-mark.svg in every ci-mark slot.
Remove deprecated ci-mark-bars fallback markup from app shells.
Keep the standard mark as dark Milo figure on white tile, also in default dark mode.
Run tests/milo-mark-consistency.ps1 when updating vendored CI assets.
Use ci-button-primary only for true primary actions.
Use plain ci-button or ci-button-secondary for normal actions.
Use ci-metric-input for prominent numeric parameter fields.
Use ci-tabs-compact when a tool has many top-level tabs.
Use assets/milo-mark.svg for Milo UI shells.
Use assets/milo/ PNG, JPG or SVG variants for documents, uploads, external previews and contexts that require fixed raster sizes.
Use alpha SVG/PNG for transparent backgrounds; use white JPG because JPEG has no alpha channel.
Run tests/milo-generated-assets.ps1 when updating vendored Milo assets.
Replace project-specific login pages with the ci-login-page and ci-login-card layout.
Use the official Milo mark in login cards.
Add apple-touch-icon, favicon and web manifest links to deployable HTML shells.
Vendor assets/apple-touch-icon.png, assets/app-icon-192.png, assets/app-icon-512.png and site.webmanifest.
Run login layout and app icon regressions before UI release.
Vendor the current favicon SVG, PNG and ICO files.
Replace old favicon links with versioned current Milo favicon links.
Keep apple-touch-icon for iPhone home screen usage.
Run tests/favicon-consistency.ps1 when updating HTML shells.

summary: Moved the visible Milo name into the official mark under the small robot.
Changed UI naming guidance so app titles use descriptive tool names without a Milo text prefix.
downstreamActions: Update vendored assets/milo-mark.svg and favicon.svg.
Remove Milo text prefixes from visible app titles such as topbar brand titles.
Keep descriptive tool names such as LEQ, Upmix or SSP Request in the UI.

summary: Added a central [hidden] override so native HTML hidden wins against ci-* component display rules.
Added a small regression demo and static test for hidden ci-workspace, ci-tabs, ci-button and ci-activity elements.
downstreamActions: Update vendored ci.css and keep [hidden] { display: none !important; } in the base layer.
Check local component CSS for selectors that override [hidden].
Use hidden-regression.html or the static PowerShell test when adapting Milo UI shells.

summary: Added a dedicated Milo chart and data visualization palette.
Documented that chart libraries must not use default colors such as brown or generic green.
downstreamActions: Map chart libraries to the --milo-chart-* tokens or pdf-tokens.json chart colors.
Replace brown, generic green, rainbow or arbitrary warm data colors with the Milo chart palette.
Use warning and danger chart colors only when the data meaning is actually warning or critical.

summary: PDF output must follow Milo CI.
Source-identifiable, consistent export names are mandatory across applications.
downstreamActions: Vendor pdf-tokens.json and apply PDF.md to report renderers.
Use correct product naming in PDF headers and metadata.
Align filenames across reports, audio and archive members; test Content-Disposition.
Render representative PDF pages, including long source names, before release.

summary: Documented deployment isolation for downstream projects.
Clarified that Milo CI local paths are for development and reference only.
Required downstream projects to copy or vendor needed CI files/assets before build or deployment.
downstreamActions: Do not keep production build imports that point to the local Milo CI project folder.
Copy or vendor required CSS files and assets into the downstream repository or build artifact path.
Verify production builds run from the downstream project without access to C:\Users\admin\Documents\ChatGPT\Milo CI.

summary: Added authentication UX/security rule for Milo apps.
Added topbar logout button styling.
Added default idle timeout guidance.
downstreamActions: If the app has authentication, add a visible .ci-logout-button to .ci-topbar-meta.
Implement automatic logout after 30 minutes of inactivity.
Ensure logout invalidates the actual session or token, not only the current UI view.

summary: Changed selected segmented button states from dark ink to Milo teal.
Added selected-state tokens for downstream apps.
downstreamActions: Replace dark selected toggle backgrounds with var(--milo-selected-bg).
Use var(--milo-selected-text) for text on selected teal controls.
Keep dark ink backgrounds for topbars, consoles, and strong structural surfaces.

summary: Added fixed app version placement in the topbar.
Added machine-readable CI update metadata.
Documented how downstream apps should detect and apply CI changes.
downstreamActions: Add .ci-topbar-meta around .ci-status and .ci-version in every app topbar.
Show the app version as vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH in .ci-version.
When checking for global CI updates, compare VERSION or ciVersion in ci-manifest.json.
